Search Data Structure Based Isosurface Extraction accelerates the identification of active cells for multiple isosurface queries by constructing an external index that allows the algorithm to disregard regions containing only non-active cells [S1].

The claim states that Search Data Structure Based Isosurface Extraction accelerates identification of active cells for multiple isosurface queries by constructing an external index to disregard non-active regions. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this in the section 'APPROACHES BASED ON SEARCH DATA STRUCTURES', stating: 'the use of external search structures allows speeding up the isosurface extraction process when multiple queries are performed on the same dataset. This result is achieved by creating an index on the data that permits to disregard large regions containing, for a given isovalue, only non-active cells.' All facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
supported
